sections.heading: Quick Verdict
sections.markdown:
## Quick Verdict: Which Active Ingredient Should You Pick?

Red marks (PIE) stem from damaged capillaries and require Niacinamide and Azelaic Acid. Dark brown spots (PIH) stem from melanin overproduction and require Alpha Arbutin 2% and Tranexamic Acid 3-5%.

Quick Verdict: Which Active Ingredient Should You Pick?

sections.heading: Comparison Methodology
sections.markdown:
## Dermatological Comparison & Action Mechanisms

Melanin synthesis relies on the tyrosinase enzyme. Dermatological actives like Alpha Arbutin and Tranexamic Acid block tyrosinase activity safely without destroying healthy melanocyte cells.

Dermatological Comparison & Action Mechanisms

sections.heading: Decision Criteria
sections.markdown:
## Decision Criteria for Indian Skin Types

Selection Guide: Alpha Arbutin 2% is a hydroquinone glycoside safe for daily long-term use in Indian skin. Tranexamic Acid 3%-5% blocks UV-triggered melanogenesis.

Decision Criteria for Indian Skin Types

sections.heading: Side By Side Matrix
sections.markdown:
## Side-by-Side Comparison Matrix

Alpha Arbutin 2% targets brown PIH dark marks. Tranexamic Acid 3%-5% targets UV and melasma spots. Kojic Acid 1%-2% brightens post-acne pigmentation.

| Active Ingredient | Concentration | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Alpha Arbutin | 2% | Stubborn brown PIH marks |
| Tranexamic Acid | 3% - 5% | UV & hormonal pigmentation |
| Kojic Acid | 1% - 2% | Post-acne dark spot brightening |

Side-by-Side Comparison Matrix

sections.heading: Reader Fit Tradeoffs
sections.markdown:
## How To Layer Both Actives Safely

Apply Alpha Arbutin 2% serum morning and night after cleansing, followed by a non-comedogenic ceramide moisturizer and broad-spectrum SPF 50 sunscreen daily.

How To Layer Both Actives Safely

sections.heading: Trust Proof
sections.markdown:
## Clinical Safety & Dermatologist Notes

Warning: Avoid OTC triple-combination steroid creams (such as Melacare or No Scars) as they cause skin thinning, steroid rosacea, and irreversible ochronosis.
